ayahs.1: Nun. By the pen and what they write—
ayahs.2: by the grace of your Lord, you are not insane.
ayahs.3: You will certainly have a reward that never ends.
ayahs.4: You are truly of outstanding character.
ayahs.5: Soon you and those who reject you will see
ayahs.6: which of you is truly misguided.
ayahs.7: Your Lord alone knows best who has strayed from His Way and who is rightly guided.
ayahs.8: So do not yield to the deniers.
ayahs.9: They wish you would compromise so they too might yield.
ayahs.10: Do not obey every habitual oath-breaker,
ayahs.13: brute—and on top of all that, one of illegitimate birth.
ayahs.14: Simply because he has been given wealth and children,
ayahs.15: whenever Our revelations are recited to him he says: 'Ancient fables!'
ayahs.16: We will soon brand him on the snout.
ayahs.17: We tested those Meccans as We tested the owners of the garden—when they swore to harvest all its fruit by early morning,
ayahs.18: making no allowance for Allah's Will.
ayahs.19: Then a torment from your Lord struck it while they slept,
ayahs.20: and it was reduced to ashes.
ayahs.21: By daybreak they called out to one another:
ayahs.22: 'Go early to your harvest if you want to pick all the fruit.'
ayahs.23: So they went off whispering to one another:
ayahs.24: 'Do not let any poor person enter your garden today.'
ayahs.25: They proceeded early, fixated on their plan.
ayahs.26: But when they saw it devastated, they cried: 'We must have lost our way!'
ayahs.27: In fact, we have been deprived of our livelihood.
ayahs.28: The most sensible among them said: 'Did I not urge you to say in sha' Allah—if Allah wills?'
ayahs.29: They replied: 'Glory be to our Lord! We have truly been wrongdoers.'
ayahs.30: Then they turned on each other, blaming one another.
ayahs.31: They said: 'Woe to us! We have certainly been transgressors.'
ayahs.32: We trust our Lord will give us a better garden than this—we are turning to Him with hope.
ayahs.33: That is how We punish in this world. The punishment of the Akhirah is far worse, if only they knew.
ayahs.34: The righteous will have the Gardens of Bliss with their Lord.
ayahs.35: Should We then treat those who submit like the wicked?
ayahs.36: What is wrong with you? How do you judge?
ayahs.37: Or do you have a scripture in which you read
ayahs.38: that you will have whatever you choose?
ayahs.39: Or do you have oaths binding on Us until the Day of Judgment that you will get whatever you decide?
ayahs.40: Ask them which of them can guarantee all that.
ayahs.41: Or do they have associate-gods? Then let them bring their associates, if what they say is true.
ayahs.42: Beware of the Day the Shin will be bared and the wicked will be asked to prostrate but will not be able to.
ayahs.43: With eyes downcast, covered in disgrace—they were called to prostrate in the world when they were fully able, but chose not to.
ayahs.44: So leave to Me those who reject this message. We will draw them gradually to destruction in ways they cannot comprehend.
ayahs.45: I only delay their end for a while, but My planning is flawless.
ayahs.46: Or are you asking them for a reward that burdens them with debt?
ayahs.47: Or do they have access to the unseen, so they copy it for all to see?
ayahs.48: So be patient with your Lord's decree, and do not be like the Man of the Whale, who cried out in total distress.
ayahs.49: Had his Lord not shown him grace, he would have been cast onto the open shore, still blameworthy.
ayahs.50: Then his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous.
ayahs.51: The those who reject the truth would almost strike you down with their eyes when they hear the Reminder, and say: 'He is certainly mad.'
ayahs.52: But it is only a Reminder for all the worlds.
